name: Maastricht University NL-High Potential Scholarship
duration: 13 months for a one-year master's; 25 months for a two-year master's
eligibleNationalities: Open to nationals of countries outside the EU/EEA, Switzerland and Surinam who do not also hold an EU/EEA or Swiss nationality, and who meet the requirements for a Dutch entry visa and residence permit. Bangladeshi nationals qualify.
ageLimit: Not older than 35 years of age on 1 September 2026
minGPA: GPA of 7.5 out of 10 or higher (equivalent to at least 75% of the maximum grade, or 3 out of 4)
applicationFee: Free for the scholarship application; however the master's programme itself may require a handling fee (not covered by UM) payable by 8 December 2025
fundingCovers: Tuition fees (paid at cost by UM International Services Desk)
monthlyStipend: EUR 1,550 per month (EUR 20,150 over 13 months, or EUR 38,750 over 25 months)
bondObligation: No financial bond; awardees must agree to become an active UM NL High Potential and UM ambassador during and after their studies, committing to at least one information session.
benefits: Tuition fees paid at cost by the UM International Services Desk
Monthly living stipend of EUR 1,550 (EUR 20,150 over 13 months for a 1-year master's, or EUR 38,750 over 25 months for a 2-year master's)
Health & liability insurance (EUR 700), arranged and paid by UM
Visa application costs paid at cost by UM
Mandatory two-week UM Pre-Academic Training costs covered
International Student Ambassador Programme (ISAP) for the first block
requiredDocuments: Curriculum vitae (up-to-date, max two A4 pages, listing awards/prizes)
Letter of motivation (using the official UM scholarship motivation-letter template)
Proof of academic excellence: university transcript / official document showing most recent GPA of 7.5/10 or higher, plus a document explaining your grade system
Personal statement of financial needs (explaining personal circumstances such as financial difficulty, caretaking responsibilities, medical condition, disability, refugee status, etc.)
A reference letter (from a former/current professor, lecturer or employer — not a family member; dated no earlier than February 2025; following the UM reference-letter guidelines)
Contact details of one referee (relationship to applicant, work phone with country code, and a work/institutional email address)

timeline.opens: Master's programme application via Studielink must be submitted before 8 December 2025; scholarship application form opens after admission
timeline.deadline: 1 February 2026 (scholarship); master's-programme admission application deadline 8 December 2025
timeline.resultsBy: April-May 2026 (status of selected / waitlisted / rejected communicated by beginning of May 2026 at the latest)
timeline.notes: Dates are for the 2026-2027 cycle (the most recent documented cycle as of 2026-06). As of the verification date the official page states 'Applications are closed and will reopen in October 2026' for the 2027-2028 cycle; participating-programme applications for 2027-2028 can be submitted from 1 October 2026. Scholarship amounts are subject to change for 2027-2028.

acceptanceRate.source: Maastricht University official scholarship page: 'Please note, this is a very competitive scholarship, only 2% of the applicants get awarded the scholarship.' — https://www.maastrichtuniversity.nl/studeren/toelating-inschrijving/financing-your-studies/scholarships/maastricht-university-nl-high (accessed 2026-06-18)

mustKnow: Two-step process: you must first apply and be admitted to a participating UM master's programme via Studielink before 8 December 2025, then submit the separate scholarship application form (with your UM student ID) by 1 February 2026.
Only specific 'participating programmes' are eligible — check the UM participating-programmes PDF for your target academic year before applying.
Age limit: you must not be older than 35 on 1 September 2026.
Minimum GPA of 7.5/10 (>=75% of the maximum, or 3/4) is a hard cutoff — applications below this are not considered.
Highly competitive: UM officially states only 2% of applicants are awarded the scholarship (21 scholarships per academic year).

An allocated room is a mandatory part of the award — refusing the room cancels the scholarship, and the accommodation is not suitable for partners/spouses or children (does not cover dependents). Housing (~EUR 960/month) is paid out of the living stipend, not a separate free benefit.
Air tickets/travel to the Netherlands are NOT covered and must be paid by the candidate.
You can submit only one application, for one scholarship only; documents cannot be added or replaced after submission.
Awardees must complete the mandatory two-week UM Pre-Academic Training (starts first week of August 2026) and agree to act as a UM ambassador.
Selected candidates are invited to an online interview before final decisions.

You must never have participated in a degree-seeking higher-education programme in the Netherlands (completed exchange programmes are fine); preference goes to candidates who have not yet obtained a master's degree.
Any programme-level handling fee is the applicant's responsibility and is not covered by UM.
renewalConditions: Awarded for the nominal duration of the master's (13 or 25 months); continued enrolment in the admitted UM master's programme is required.
languageRequirements: Set by the specific UM master's programme's admission requirements (typically IELTS/TOEFL for English-taught programmes); the scholarship itself adds no separate language test. Verify on the chosen programme's webpage.
standardizedTests: Not required by the scholarship; any test requirement is set by the individual master's programme.
